sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant - original claimant, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 23.07.2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Panchmahal at Godhra in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1315 of 2007, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.29,000/- with 9% per annum interest to the claimant, holding the opponents no.2 and 3 are liable jointly and severally and further the tribunal has failed to appreciate the fact that the claimant was a minor aged 10 years, who had sustained 10% physical NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2129/2022 ORDER DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined disability.

sentences.text: Mr. Nishit Bhalodi, learned advocate appearing for the appellant submits that learned tribunal ought to have followed the judgment of Master Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited and another reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396 and should have considered the case of Kum. Michael Vs. Regional Manager, The Oriental Insurance Company Limited & Ors. reported in JT 2013 (3) SC 311 and following the yardstick laid down in Master Mallikarjun (supra), the tribunal should have granted the compensation to the minor.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Countering the argument, Ms. Vyoma Jhaveri, learned advocate appearing for the GSRTC has submitted that the learned tribunal has considered 4% permanent disability for body as a whole and hence, the notional income of the minor has been considered, and stated accordingly, the calculation is consistent with the amount granted under the head of Pain Shock and Suffering and other compensation.
Thus, it is submitted by Ms. Jhaveri that no interference would be NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2129/2022 ORDER DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined required by this Court to the amount so far granted.

4. In case of Master Mallikarjun (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that while considering the claim by a victim child, it would be unfair and improper to follow the structured formula as per the Second Schedule to the Motor Vehicles Act for reasons more than one.
The Apex court thus considering the fact that for children there is no income.
A child cannot be equated to such a non-earning person.

Therefore, the compensation is to be worked out under the non- pecuniary heads in addition to the actual amounts incurred for treatment done and/or to be done,
transportation, assistance of attendant, etc.

It has been laid down that the main elements of damage in the case of child victims are the pain, shock, frustration, deprivation of ordinary pleasures and enjoyment associated with healthy and mobile limbs.
The compensation awarded should enable the child to acquire something or to develop a lifestyle which will offset to some extent the inconvenience or discomfort arising out of the disability.
Appropriate compensation for disability should take care of all the non-pecuniary damages.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2129/2022 ORDER DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined 5.
In this case, the disability of the minor claimant was assessed by the doctor in view of the sustained fracture on knee joint as 10% partial, permanent disability of left lower limb.
However, by way of pursis at Exh.21, both the parties had agreed to considered 4% negligence of body as a whole.

In Master Mallikarjun (supra) the different yardstick have been laid down, which is reproduced herein-above:-
"12.

Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts,
we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; upto 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; upto 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs.6 lakhs.

For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Re.1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take Nitaben Parsingbhai Baria (Bhil) vs Kanabhai Kalubhai Bariya on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142987834/
2 different yardstick.

entities.text: Nitaben Parsingbhai Baria (Bhil) vs Kanabhai Kalubhai Bariya
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the disability is to the tune of 18%.
Appellant had a longer period of hospitalization for about two months causing also inconvenience and loss of earning to the parents....."
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2129/2022 ORDER DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined 6.

The permanent disability has been assessed by the doctor as 10%, while both the parties had agreed upon to consider 4% negligence of body as a whole, therefore, both the percentage are kept in mind and as per the yardstick laid down, upto disability of 10%, the claimant - victim minor child would be entitled to get compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-.
7. The medical expenses has been considered as Rs.2,500/- and Rs.5,000/- has been granted under the head of transportation, attendance charges and special diet.

Therefore, the claimant - victim child would be entitled to get the following final amount as competition:-
 Particulars Amount (Rs.)
 Pain, Shock & Suffering 1,00,000/-
 Medical Expenses 2,500/-
 Transportation, Attendance Charges 5,000/-
 & Special Diet  Total 1,07,500/-
8.
The learned tribunal has granted Rs.29,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum, against the GSRTC, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2129/2022 ORDER DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined required to be deposited.
The enhanced amount would come to Rs.78,500/-, which the GSRTC shall deposit within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of the writ of the order.
It is directed that the enhanced amount would be paid with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of the claim petition till realization.
9. In the facts and circumstances, the present appeal is partly allowed, with no order as to costs.

The judgment and award dated 23.07.2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.),
Panchmahal at Godhra in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1315 of 2007 shall stand modified as aforesaid.
